back: A voluntary association of people who jointly own and democratically control a business to meet shared needs.

Open membership; democratic control (one member, one vote); economic participation (limited interest, surplus by trade); independence; education; co-operation among co-operatives; concern for community.
Common need → first meeting and interim committee → viability study → by-laws → registration with the registrar → shares sold → AGM elects committee.
Producer, marketing, supply (input), savings and credit, multipurpose.
Bulk buying, bargaining power, shared facilities, credit, training, democratic control, surplus returned to members.
Poor management, little capital, dishonesty, low commitment and side-selling, late payment, conflict, outside interference.
Part of the surplus returned to members in proportion to their trade with the co-operative.
Co-operative: one member, one vote. Company: votes by number of shares.
